newsitem.title: ITALY: Bossi urges release of Venice belltower raiders.
newsitem.headline: Bossi urges release of Venice belltower raiders.

text.p: Umberto Bossi, firebrand leader of the Northern League, on Friday called for the release of eight men jailed for storming the belltower in Venice's St Mark's Square in a separatist stunt.

Bossi told reporters the League had started gathering signatures for a petition seeking the release of the eight which will be presented to Italy's parliament, President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro and to the European Court of Justice.

A court jailed the eight men on Wednesday -- four of them for six years and the others for four years and six months -- and also ordered them to pay 150 million lire ($88,000) in damages to the Venice town council.
The eight smashed their way into the belltower at night after hijacking a ferry to take them and a ramshackle armoured car down the Grand Canal to the square in the lagoon city.

Calling themselves soldiers of the "Most Serene Republic" of Venice, a centuries-old maritime power before its fall 200 years ago, the eight unfurled a flag of the republic and shouted separatist slogans.

"Free them immediately," said Bossi, who is seeking the creation of an independent state of "Padania" in Italy's prosperous north. "The people of Padania do not agree with the decision of the Venice magistrates," he said.
Bossi is himself on trial on charges of incitement to violence for urging his followers to take action against those who voted for Italy's far-right National Alliance party.
